method: First-pass verse-by-verse screening from Qur'an 2:271–280 and identified biblical passage translations. Hebrew/Greek critical editions and manuscript witnesses not collated. Candidate sources are unpublished and require independent verification. Do not infer borrowing.

verses.finding: Public almsgiving acceptable; concealed gifts to poor preferred; Matthew 6:1–4 emphasizes secrecy and warns against giving for display.
Guidance belongs to God; spending for God's sake benefits the giver; no precise earlier textual counterpart established.
Alms for restrained poor unable to travel and unwilling to beg; no precise earlier counterpart established.
Giving by night/day and secretly/openly; thematic continuity with 2:271 but no independent precise earlier counterpart established.
Condemns riba and distinguishes trade from riba; compare earlier Israelite interest restrictions, not identical legal scope.
God destroys riba and increases charitable giving; no specific prior textual match verified.
Faith, prayer and almsgiving with divine recompense; broad scriptural motifs, no distinct specific parallel established.
Command to relinquish remaining riba; compare Deuteronomy 23:19–20 as legal contrast with different group scope.
Warning of conflict for continued riba and preservation of principal on repentance; no identical earlier legal formulation established.
Grant an insolvent debtor respite; voluntary debt remission commended; compare Exodus 22:25–27 and Leviticus 25:35–37 on protecting poor borrowers, but no exact postponement prescription there.

candidates.difference: Matthew warns specifically against performative public charity; Qur'an explicitly allows public giving while preferring concealed gifts to poor.

candidates.shared: Restrictions on interest and protection of financially vulnerable people
candidates.difference: Leviticus specifies an impoverished fellow Israelite in covenantal law; Qur'an 2:275 distinguishes trading and riba and includes resurrection/judgment imagery.

candidates.shared: Prohibits charging interest in a specified setting
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy distinguishes fellow Israelites from foreigners; Qur'anic command does not state that exception.

candidates.shared: Protects impoverished debtors against exploitative lending
candidates.difference: Exodus restricts interest and mandates return of a pledged garment; Qur'an 2:280 orders delay for hardship and commends remission.
